canonicalizer: rfc8785@0.1.4 (Python) / canonicalize@3.0.0 (TypeScript) / gowebpki/jcs v1.0.1 (Go) / cyberphone/json-canonicalization (Java) / serde_jcs@0.2.0 (Rust)

anchored_to.ietf_id: draft-hopley-x402-compliance-receipt-00 (Independent Submission, Informational; submitted to IETF datatracker 2026-05-23)
load_bearing_invariants: screen_result is a closed enumeration of {ALLOW, REFER, DENY}; each value produces a byte-distinct content_hash from the other two.
jurisdiction_flags is an ordered list; reordering the array elements produces a different content_hash (arrays are byte-load-bearing under RFC 8785).
canon_version is an in-band pin; changing the pin value produces a different content_hash.
screen_timestamp_ms is an epoch-millisecond integer (Substrate Rule 2). RFC 3339 string forms are rejected at validation time by the substrate's build_compliance_receipt primitive.
Audit chain rows link via prev_hash. Row N's prev_hash MUST equal row N-1's row_content_hash; row 1's prev_hash MUST be 64 zero hex characters.
anchored_to.spec_authorship: AlgoVoi-authored. The receipt format and canonicalisation discipline are specified in draft-hopley-x402-compliance-receipt-00 (Sections 3, 4, 5).

derivation: Eight receipt-shape vectors split into three groups: (A) baseline three-state coverage of the closed enumeration (ALLOW, REFER, DENY) with otherwise identical fields, proving the screen_result field is byte-load-bearing -- this is the load-bearing property under UK POCA 2002 Section 330 where a REFER outcome can trigger a Suspicious Activity Report obligation that a DENY does not; (B) array-order probe demonstrating that jurisdiction_flags is byte-load-bearing under RFC 8785 (arrays are not sorted during canonicalisation); (C) canon_version pin probe demonstrating that the in-band canonicalisation rule pin is byte-load-bearing. Three additional audit-chain-row vectors (006-008) demonstrate the chain linkage property: each row's prev_hash equals the previous row's row_content_hash, with row 1 anchoring to all-zero.

ietf_id_section_anchors.001-baseline-ALLOW: draft-hopley-x402-compliance-receipt-00 Section 3 (Receipt Format Specification), Section 4 (Canonicalisation), Appendix A.1

verification_recipe: 1. For each receipt vector (001 through 005), take the receipt object verbatim.
2. Canonicalise under RFC 8785 (any of the five reference impls).
3. base64-encode the JCS bytes; MUST equal expected_jcs_bytes_b64.
4. SHA-256 the JCS bytes, lowercase hex; MUST equal expected_content_hash.
5. For chain rows (006 through 008), repeat steps 2-4 on the row object; the result MUST equal expected_row_content_hash.
6. Verify pair invariants: pair-001 to pair-005 MUST all hold (different_hash_from).
7. Verify chain linkage: row 1 prev_hash is 64 zeros; row 2 prev_hash equals row 1 row_content_hash; row 3 prev_hash equals row 2 row_content_hash.

pair_semantics.closed_enum_byte_load_bearing: MUST differ (screen_result varies across the closed three-element enumeration)
pair_semantics.array_order_byte_load_bearing: MUST differ (jurisdiction_flags array order is not normalised by JCS)
pair_semantics.canon_version_pin_byte_load_bearing: MUST differ (canon_version is a byte-significant in-band field)
pair_semantics.chain_linkage: each row's prev_hash MUST equal the previous row's row_content_hash

vectors.description: Baseline ALLOW receipt. Reference compliance screening receipt with the categorical outcome ALLOW; all other fields are the fixed baseline.

REFER receipt. All fields identical to vector 001 except screen_result is REFER. Demonstrates that the closed enumeration is byte-load-bearing; under UK POCA 2002 Section 330 a REFER outcome can carry a Suspicious Activity Report obligation that a DENY does not, and the categorical distinction is preserved at the canonical-bytes level rather than collapsed.
DENY receipt. All fields identical to vector 001 except screen_result is DENY. Together with vectors 001 and 002, completes the three-state coverage of the closed enumeration.

Array-reorder probe. All fields identical to vector 001 except jurisdiction_flags is ['EU', 'UK'] instead of ['UK', 'EU']. Demonstrates that array element order is byte-load-bearing in the canonical form: JCS RFC 8785 does not normalise array order.

canon_version pin probe. All fields identical to vector 001 except canon_version is jcs-rfc8785-v2 (hypothetical successor pin). Demonstrates that the canonicalisation-rule pin is byte-load-bearing: a successor canon_version produces a different content_hash even when the rest of the receipt content is unchanged.

Audit chain row 1. First row of a three-row hash-linked chain anchoring the receipts in vectors 001, 002, 003. The row's prev_hash is the all-zero anchor (the chain has no predecessor); the row's receipt_content_hash references vector 001's content_hash.
Audit chain row 2. Second row of the three-row chain. The row's prev_hash MUST equal row 1's row_content_hash; the row's receipt_content_hash references vector 002's content_hash.

Audit chain row 3. Third row of the three-row chain. The row's prev_hash MUST equal row 2's row_content_hash; the row's receipt_content_hash references vector 003's content_hash. A verifier walking the chain confirms the linkage property end-to-end.

pair_invariants.description: closed enum byte-load-bearing: ALLOW differs from REFER under otherwise-identical receipts

POCA s.330 SAR-distinction byte-load-bearing: REFER differs from DENY under otherwise-identical receipts (the categorical distinction is preserved at the canonical-bytes level rather than collapsed by scoring or tier projection)
closed enum byte-load-bearing: ALLOW differs from DENY under otherwise-identical receipts
jurisdiction_flags array order byte-load-bearing: ['UK','EU'] differs from ['EU','UK'] under otherwise-identical receipts (JCS RFC 8785 does not normalise array order)
canon_version pin byte-load-bearing: jcs-rfc8785-v1 differs from jcs-rfc8785-v2 under otherwise-identical receipts

chain_invariants.description: row 1 prev_hash is the all-zero anchor (chain has no predecessor)
row 2 prev_hash equals row 1 row_content_hash (chain linkage)
row 3 prev_hash equals row 2 row_content_hash (chain linkage)
